summary.text: A 72-year-old Caucasian woman, a former 30-pack-year smoker who quit 25 years before, was referred to the respiratory clinic with a 6-month history of exertional breathlessness and yearly chest infections. She had polymyalgia rheumatica on 1 mg prednisolone and no history of childhood respiratory problems or asbestosis. Oxygen saturation was 95% on room air and spirometry showed an obstructive pattern.

An initial chest radiograph 2 years before presentation suggested increased radiolucency of the left lung; serial radiographs 2 years later showed an unchanged left hemithorax with progressive right-sided peripheral opacification and volume loss. Contrast-enhanced CT showed a hypoplastic left pulmonary artery, attenuated peripheral branches, a hyperinflated left lung with air trapping and cystic bronchiectasis, and a small right lung with subpleural reticulation, traction bronchiectasis and ground-glass opacification. PET CT showed reduced FDG uptake in the left lung.

Sputum culture grew pseudomonas species and right-lung bronchoalveolar lavage showed mixed cellularity with 22% eosinophils and 36% neutrophils; eosinophilic pneumonia was not suspected. CT features were in keeping with Swyer-James-MacLeod syndrome in the left lung, diagnosed after the age of 70 years; right-lung findings suggested an underlying pulmonary fibrosis, which the authors label idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

ambiguities.issue: The CT text says the right-lung findings suggest an underlying pulmonary fibrosis, while the abstract, discussion and learning points state idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis as the diagnosis. No biopsy, multidisciplinary discussion or clinical-radiological criteria for IPF are reported, so the condition is recorded as provisional.

evidence.quote: suggesting an underlying pulmonary fibrosis
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis affecting the contralateral lung
in this case the coexistence of SJMS with IPF

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer a histological or multidisciplinary confirmation of IPF, or an exclusion of other fibrosing diseases.

ambiguities.issue: The paragraph reports a 6-month history of exertional breathlessness yet also states that exercise tolerance was unlimited and she enjoyed good health.

evidence.quote: a 6-month history of exertional breathlessness
Her exercise tolerance was unlimited and she enjoyed a good health.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not resolve the difference or infer a functional grade or timing for either statement.

ambiguities.issue: The paragraph says she was on prednisolone 1 mg for polymyalgia rheumatica but "not on any regular medications" otherwise; whether prednisolone was still being taken at presentation is not stated.

ambiguities.issue: The authors say the 2-year-prior radiograph suggested left-lung radiolucency; the relation of "2 years later" radiographs to the presentation date is only stated relative to the initial radiograph.

ambiguities.issue: The authors state eosinophilic pneumonia was not suspected despite a high lavage eosinophil count, and that it is difficult to tell whether the affected left lung is larger, normal or smaller than the contralateral fibrotic lung; neither is a measured result.

ambiguities.issue: The discussion proposes that SJMS is "protective" against IPF in the affected lung; this is an authors' hypothesis, not a patient finding.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the 3 JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.
No treatment, follow-up or outcome is reported for the patient.

IPF is stated as the diagnosis by the authors while the case text only says the CT findings suggest underlying pulmonary fibrosis; no biopsy or multidisciplinary confirmation is reported (recorded as provisional).

No dates are given; the only anchors are 2 years before presentation (initial radiograph), 2 years later (serial radiographs), 25 years before presentation (smoking cessation) and a 6-month symptom history.
Reference ranges and predicted values are not given; percentages in parentheses after FEV1 and FVC are kept as printed without the source naming them predicted values.
Discussion statements about SJMS, IPF pathobiology, incidence and literature cases are background, not patient facts.
